answer: Sybil resistance is priced as vesting capital. Each identity locks a 25x expected-reward bond; the kernel contract releases it in 20 epoch tranches, payable only if the identity co-signed a VRF-drawn verification role. Witnesses reject claims lacking that co-signature, and the vesting clock binds to the immutable registration slot, so one bond cannot split across clones. Minting n identities freezes 25x*n units for 20 epochs against 1x per clone: linear negative carry. Like juniper rings densifying slowly, trust accrues by audited time; jade scarcity is the toll fakes pay.
